figures.title: Selective delegation in the LangGraph workflow
figures.caption: A reader-oriented diagram of the selective path. Failed conditions cannot release an order; review requests are recorded, and no human resolution is simulated. The full executable graph is exported separately as architecture_graph.mmd.

figures.title: Model calls per replenishment decision
figures.caption: Calls include every attempted native model call. The same model and generation settings were used. Structured-table parsing is a declared architectural route, not a reused model response.

figures.title: Mean time per replenishment decision
figures.caption: Measured whole-decision blocks, including graph orchestration and the numerical tool. Fixed/selective order was counterbalanced. This describes the experimental instance, not employee time or production cost.

figures.title: Correct application of the declared business priority
figures.caption: Accuracy is scored against the policy available before ordering. Active promotion covers days 2–6. Explicit policy routing does not demonstrate that the model itself improved its reasoning.

figures.title: Inventory-performance change relative to the fixed workflow
figures.caption: Points show paired simulation-seed means; intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals for 30 simulated seeds. Positive values favour selective delegation in both panels. Costs are synthetic inventory operating-cost indices, not realised savings.

figures.title: Expiry outcomes by RetailNet operating situation
figures.caption: Hypothetical three-day FIFO stock process. A service or cost improvement does not necessarily imply less waste. M5 has no expiry within the evaluated horizon.
